nary_nodes.label: AI-enabled cyberattack on Taiwan
evidence: Hackers deployed an AI system to carry out sophisticated cyberattacks on Taiwan, officials said, in what experts believe is the first known fully autonomous attack on government agencies.

Over four days in July, the AI agents were able to map 21 government systems, crack 85 government user accounts, and extract 2,500 personnel records, according to Dream, an Israeli AI firm that first discovered the attack.
The attack also extended to Taiwan’s nuclear safety agency and the government’s IT vendors as well as at least seven other energy sector companies.
nary_nodes.type_definition: A cyberattack carried out with the assistance or enablement of artificial intelligence.
nary_nodes.type_justification: No schema.org class directly represents an 'AIEnabledCyberattack'. It is a specific type of Cyberattack (defined in E33 as an Event).

nary_nodes.label: Hacker system automated intrusion
evidence: The hackers’ system was built using open-source AI agents to automate and coordinate much of the intrusion, including reconnaissance, credential attacks and strategizing subsequent attack paths, Dream said.
